title: Definition of clinical subtypes of sepsis and septic shock using statistical analysis of digital patient records.
summary: This study analyzes existing electronic hospital records of patients with sepsis or septic shock to identify groups of patients with similar disease patterns. By defining such subtypes, future treatments may be tailored more precisely to individual patient groups. The study is purely retrospective and does not involve any additional tests or interventions.
conditions: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome of infectious origin with organ failure

interventions.name: Retrospective, single-center cohort of adult intensive care patients meeting Sepsis-3 criteria for sepsis or septic shock. Data are exclusively derived from pseudonymized electronic patient records extracted from the institutional electronic health records (EHR). No interventions or additional proce

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Admission to an intensive care unit at the study center during the defined study period
Age ≥ 18 years
Fulfillment of Sepsis-3 criteria for sepsis or septic shock
Clinical suspicion of infection with initiation of antibiotic therapy and blood culture sampling
Organ dysfunction defined by SOFA score ≥ 2
Availability of relevant routine clinical data in the PDMS (vital signs, laboratory parameters, medications, longitudinal data)
Exclusion criteria:
incomplete or missing core clinical data precluding statistical analysis or subtype classification
Duplicate patient entries (only first ICU admission considered)
Age < 18 years
Withdrawal of consent for secondary use of clinical data, if applicable under data protection regulations
